proposals.name: Alex Turner
proposals.quote: Alex Turner received his B.S. In Mechanical Engineering in 2025 with a focus in mechatronics, completed at the University of Washington. He began his masters in Mechanical Engineering in 2025 before transitioning into the PHD program in 2026, both at the UW. Following his senior year capstone project on a medical rehabilitation device, Alex has continued work on the application of robotics in medical settings.
proposals.note: Explicit transition into UW PhD2026; prior BS/MS2025 not reused as doctoral date.

proposals.name: Navneet Kaur
proposals.quote: Navneet Kaur obtained her Bachelor of Technology in Mechanical Engineering with a minor in Robotics from the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IIT Gandhinagar) in 2022. She received her Masters in Mechanical Engineering degree from the University of Washinton (UW) in 2024 and has now transitioned into pursuing a PhD at UW. Her research interests are centered on advancing optimal control techniques in complex dynamical systems.

proposals.name: Michael Bi
proposals.quote: Michael Bi received his B.S. in Mechanical Engineering from Purdue University in 2023, before beginning his Ph.D. at the University of Washington later that year. His current research focuses on optimizing human-robot interaction in shared autonomy systems.
proposals.note: Explicit UWPhD began later2023, separately from PurdueBS; only stated startpoint retained.

proposals.name: William Howe
proposals.quote: William Howe received a B.S. and M.S. in Aerospace Engineering from California Polytechnic State University. He then spent a decade working in the aerospace industry, which culminated in him being in charge of the Mechanical Systems team for the first human flight of Blue Origin's New Shepard rocket. He joined the Ph.D. program in 2023 and is currently researching mutli-agent robotics and information propagation in the presence of perception constraints.
proposals.note: Explicit joinedPhD2023; only stated startpoint retained.

proposals.name: Aaron Weber
proposals.quote: Aaron Weber received his B.S. in Electrical Engineering (minor in Applied Mathematics) from Gonzaga University in 2021, and started at UW as a Master's student that same year before transitioning to the PhD program in 2023. His research interests include multi-agent robotics, communications in robotic networks, odor localization, and bio-inspired robotics. He is working jointly with Prof. Sawyer Fuller.

proposals.name: Henry Chang
proposals.quote: Henry Chang Chang received his B.S. in Civil Engineering (minor in Mechanical Engineering) from National Cheng Kung University in 2017, and his M.S. in Mechanical Engineering from the University of California San Diego in 2020. Prior to his Ph.D. study, he worked for 1.5 years at Industrial Technology Research Institution (ITRI) as an autonomous driving engineer. He started his Ph.D. in 2022 with research interests in multi-agent robotics, data-driven control, and decision-making.

supporting_sources.quote: Wade Marquette works at Amazon (2025) received a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering (2019) and an M.S. in Mechanical Engineering (2021) from the University of Washington. His graduated with a PhD from the University of Washington's Mechanical Engineering department, where his research focused on robotics for confined space manufacturing in collaboration with the Boeing Advanced Research Center (BARC). During his PhD work, he developed and patented robots while conducting controls research to simplify robot teleoperation. Wade joined Amazon as a Postdoctoral Scientist in early 2025 and became an Amazon Innovation Engineer (2026) in the Worldwide Engineering and Innovation team, where he develops automated material handling equipment and robotic technologies for Amazon's delivery stations.

proposals.name: Lance McCann
proposals.quote: Lance McCann works at Amazon (2026). He has three degrees from the University of Washington, receiving his BSME in 2000, his Masters in Applied Physics in 2008, and PhD in 2024. As part of his Masters program, Lance developed technology for Magnetic Resonance Force Microscopy. Lance worked five years as an applications engineer for Pacific Machine Automation, where he developed automated equipment for a wide variety of industrial applications. Since 2006, he has worked for the Boeing Company developing automated technology for the fabrication and assembly of composite structures. In 2026 he moved to Amazon. He worked jointly with Prof. Joe Garbini.

His current research interests include machine learning, user intent prediction and their applications in the control of systems. .

proposals.name: Brandon Smith
proposals.quote: Brandon Smith joined Tethers Unlimited. He received a Bachelors of Science in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Washington in 2008. He then received a Masters of Science from the University of Washington in 2009. His focus was in systems dynamics and control systems, and his research was in mixing with microfluidics. After that, he worked on hard disk drives for Western Digital Corporation for three years in their servo pattern write group. There he made contributions in spindle control and advanced servo write techniques with two patents pending. He obtained the Ph.D. degree at the University of Washington in Seattle, Washington in 2017, working jointly with Prof. Mark Tuttle. His research interests are in identification and control of heat transfer in composite materials.
